Prerequisite

pree-REK-wih-zit -- from Latin pre- ('before') + requirere ('to require'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Prerequisite is something required as a prior condition before something else can happen.

Completing Introductory Chemistry is a strict prerequisite for the advanced organic chemistry seminar.

Worked Example

A valid driver's permit is a prerequisite for signing up for the behind-the-wheel driving course.

Notice the order: you need the permit before you're even allowed to register for the course. A prerequisite always comes first, as a condition that unlocks whatever comes next.

How Prerequisite Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

requirement

requirement: something that must be met or satisfied

precondition

precondition: a formal condition that must be true beforehand

Antonyms

outcome

outcome: the result that happens at the end of a process

result

result: something that follows as a consequence

How Strong Is It? — requirement → prerequisite → precondition

requirement vs. prerequisite

requirement vs. prerequisite: Requirement is lighter than prerequisite: a requirement simply has to be met at some point, while a prerequisite blocks everything that follows until it is satisfied first.

precondition vs. prerequisite

precondition vs. prerequisite: Precondition is stronger than prerequisite: a prerequisite can be a routine box to check before a course, while a precondition is absolute — until it is met, nothing else happens at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pre-

prefix — pre-: before (Latin)

root — -requis-

root — -requis-: to require, to seek (Latin (requirere))

suffix — -ite

suffix — -ite: 'having been' (as in definite) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Prerequisite combines pre- ('before') with Latin requirere ('to require') and the -ite ending meaning 'having been,' as in definite -- literally 'required beforehand.' A prerequisite is a condition that must be satisfied first, before whatever comes next is even possible.

Use the root in a new word: requisite

Use the root in a new word: requisite: A calm, steady hand is requisite for any surgeon, no matter how many years of training they've had.
